comparison: Perfect agreement on binding kinetics measurements (C1, C2, C17, C18, C59-C61, C63, C73-C74, C82-C83). Both evaluations find the single molecule tracking measurements of association times and exponential distributions well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly praise these as 'interesting findings' and describe the data as 'more direct and believable.'

Strong agreement on 1:1 stoichiometry findings (C3, C43-C46, C52, C78). Both evaluations accept the quantitative measurements showing ~6 ZAP70 per pMHC corresponding to 1:1 stoichiometry. Peer reviewers explicitly list 'each pMHC-TCR recruits several ZAP70 molecules' as an interesting finding in this 'outstanding study.'

Agreement on downstream amplification inference (C4, C104). Both evaluations accept the logical conclusion that amplification must occur downstream given the 1:1 stoichiometry at triggering. Peer reviewers' acceptance of the stoichiometry findings implicitly supports this inference.

Agreement on technical validation of two-population observation (C10-C11, C27-C32). Both evaluations accept the bimodal distribution and technical controls. Peer reviewers praise 'technical breakthroughs' and 'nicely executed two color, single molecule experiment,' though they request additional clarification about dynamics.

Agreement on identification of slow-moving pMHC as TCR-bound complexes (C12-C14, C33-C35). Both evaluations accept the peptide specificity and spatial correlation evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through their endorsement of the overall conclusions about TCR-pMHC complexes.

Agreement on cytoskeletal engagement (C15-C16, C38-C39, C51, C76). Both evaluations accept the connection between linear trajectories and actomyosin transport. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'Virtually all pMHC-TCR complexes become immobilized and hook onto the actin cytoskeleton' as an interesting finding.

Partial disagreement on ZAP70 recruitment dynamics (C40-C42, C48, C53, C75). OpenEval finds the two-color tracking and stable association well-supported. Peer reviewers accept the basic finding but express uncertainty, specifically requesting more analysis of 'variability or successive recruitment of Zap70' and whether accumulation over time can be detected.

Agreement on individual pMHC triggering without cooperativity (C54, C77). Both evaluations accept that single molecule resolution demonstrates individual pMHC can trigger TCR. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'the TCR-pMHC act as discrete entities and do not appear to aggregate' as an interesting finding.

Agreement on lack of cooperativity and serial triggering (C79, C103). Both evaluations accept the negative results regarding these mechanisms. Peer reviewers' statement that 'TCR-pMHC act as discrete entities' supports the conclusion against cooperativity at the molecular scale.

Agreement on computational simulations against serial rebinding (C22-C23, C67-C69, C71-C72). Both evaluations accept the simulation results showing serial rebinding is unlikely. Peer reviewers implicitly endorse this through their acceptance of the overall conclusion that TCR-pMHC act as discrete entities.

Agreement on downstream feedback mechanism inference (C81). Both evaluations accept that cooperativity must arise from downstream mechanisms given the 1:1 stoichiometry. Peer reviewers' acceptance of the stoichiometry findings supports this logical inference.

Disagreement on comparison with FRET measurements (C89-C94). OpenEval finds the reporting of discrepancies and Latrunculin A effects well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge the new data are 'more direct and believable' but express uncertainty, stating 'These differences to the previously published results are puzzling and need to be discussed.'

Disagreement on temperature independence (C93-C94). OpenEval accepts the minimal effects of temperature as directly measured. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting 'There is not much of a difference between 24 and 37 degrees. This is surprising and should be discussed.'

Agreement on uncertainty regarding conformational flexibility hypothesis (C24, C95-C100). Both evaluations recognize this as speculative. OpenEval notes it remains 'untested speculation' with no direct evidence. Peer reviewers want more discussion of the contradictions this hypothesis attempts to explain.

OpenEval finds the sequence comparison and inference of similar binding kinetics (C85-C87) well-supported by sequence data and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about TCR similarity.

OpenEval accepts the overall conclusion about mass action laws (C101-C102) as a reasonable synthesis of findings. No specific peer review evaluation found for this overarching conclusion, though peer acceptance of component findings implicitly supports it.
OpenEval finds the background context claims (C5-C9) appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.

Partial disagreement on ZAP70 stoichiometry observations (C47, C49-C50). OpenEval accepts the spatial distribution and range of stoichiometries as directly observed. Peer reviewers want more detailed analysis of variability and temporal accumulation, expressing uncertainty about what can be extracted at the single molecule level.

Agreement on technical limitations (C55-C58, C10). Both evaluations accept the acknowledged limitations of the fluorescence-based approach. Peer reviewers praise the 'technical breakthroughs' and 'unique approach using low intensity light for longer time periods.'
OpenEval accepts the experimental conditions description (C36-C37) as appropriately stated and cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific experimental parameter claims.

Agreement on prior work context (C64-C66). Both evaluations accept these as appropriate representations of previous hypotheses. OpenEval notes they provide context for the authors' simulations; peer reviewers implicitly accept through endorsement of simulation conclusions.
OpenEval accepts the caveat about TCR clustering (C70) as an appropriate limitation acknowledgment. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific limitation claim.
OpenEval accepts the description of the original serial triggering model (C80) as accurate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this historical context claim.
OpenEval accepts the structural knowledge and prior hypotheses (C84, C88) as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural context claims.
